site.title: Acerola · design
site.description: Design system and project standard for every Acerola app: colors, typography, components, icon, mascot and the kit to start a project.
site.footer: acerola-sync standard · MPL-2.0 · fonts under SIL OFL 1.1

hero.title: Acerola design system
hero.lead: Colors, typography, shape, components, icon and mascot for every app, following the acerola-sync standard.

brand.title: Icon and mascot
brand.lead: The acerola is the icon: app, favicon, tab and notification. The mascot is the personality: welcome, empty state, profile and notices. Use the files as they are.

type.title: DM Sans, big and heavy
type.lead: The whole interface is DM Sans: strong text in font-black tracking-tight and numbers with tabular-nums. Noto Serif is for editorial titles and Titan One only for the brand.
type.body: Body text in DM Sans: your anime and manga list in one place, synced with AniList without burning the quota.

colors.title: One palette
colors.lead: Showing the {theme} theme: switch it at the top. Click a color to copy its value. In the interface, tokens only: never a loose hex or a Tailwind color.

shape.title: Solid blocks, no borders
shape.lead: Each role has its radius. Lift shadow for what stays still, float for what floats. State shows in the background, never in a colored border.

components.title: The sync pieces
components.lead: AcerolaChipTabs, AcerolaPillNav, AcerolaStatTile, AcerolaMediaCard and friends, also as plain CSS (.ac-*) for any stack.

icons.title: Android, iOS and web
icons.lead: Generated for the three platforms: mipmaps and adaptive icon (with a monochrome layer) on Android, AppIcon on iOS and favicon, PWA and maskable on the web.
icons.note: The app icon is the acerola. The mascot pack exists for avatars and social media, not for the home screen.

usage.title: Straight from the URL
usage.lead: Everything here is public and has a fixed address. The addresses below already point to this server.

downloads.title: Take it all
downloads.lead: The zips are built on every release from the files on this page.

accent.title: Accent
accent.note: One primary action per screen. Text on a solid color uses its -foreground.

surface.title: Surfaces and text
surface.note: From the deepest to the highest. Solid blocks, no colored borders.

state.title: State
state.note: -soft is the background and the tone is the text: success badge = success-soft + success.

chart.title: Charts
chart.note: One color per series, in this order.

rules.use: Text, buttons, lists, fields, titles and numbers
Editorial title: post, section cover, document
rules.rare: Used sparingly; the interface stays in DM Sans

rules.use: Lettering, hero, splash, cover, tape and sticker
rules.size: Always uppercase and big (32px or more)
rules.never: Never in a button, tab, field, list or screen title

icon.title: Icon (acerola)
icon.use: The app icon: favicon, tab, notification and logo in the bar.

mascot.title: Mascot
mascot.use: Welcome, empty state, profile, avatar and notices. Never as an app icon.

plate.title: Icon with background
plate.use: Image only (README, post, cover). Never as an app icon: use the foreground for that.

mono.title: Monochrome icon
mono.use: Android 13+ themed icon and single-color uses.

brand.title: Full kit
brand.text: Everything on this page: icon, mascot, app icons, fonts, css, tokens and the skills.

template.title: Project standard
template.text: Kit for the root of a new repository: skills, hooks, lefthook, scripts, GitHub and the MPL-2.0 license.

skills.title: Claude Code skills
skills.text: acerola-design, acerola-project and acerola-git: unzip into ~/.claude/skills/.

logos.title: Icon and mascot
logos.text: Icon SVGs (normal, foreground, background, mono) and the mascot, plus the PNGs.

icons.title: App icons
icons.text: Android (mipmaps and adaptive), iOS (AppIcon) and web (favicon, PWA).

css.title: CSS and tokens
css.text: tokens.css, theme.css, tailwind.css, components.css and acerola.css, with the fonts.

fonts.title: Fonts
fonts.text: DM Sans, Noto Serif and Titan One as woff2, with their licenses (OFL).

examples.title: Components in HTML
examples.lead: Each piece with the HTML that builds it. All it needs is acerola.css (or tailwind.css + components.css). Switch the theme at the top to see both modes.

heading.title: Screen title
heading.note: A big, heavy word with the small line above. The types (Anime/Manga) are the title words themselves.

buttons.title: Buttons (AcerolaButton)
buttons.note: font-black pill. Primary on primary, secondary on surface, contrast on a colored background.

tabs.title: Chips (AcerolaChipTabs)
tabs.note: Track on surface; the active one inverts to foreground. Small count with tabular-nums.

nav.title: Navigation (AcerolaPillNav)
nav.note: Floating pill with shadow-float; the active item becomes a primary pill with its name.

stats.title: Numbers (AcerolaStatTile)
stats.note: rounded-tile block in the tone: soft background and tone text. Small uppercase label.

covers.title: Cover (AcerolaMediaCard)
covers.note: 2/3 aspect in rounded-tile; chip over scrim, shade at the bottom and progress in primary.

badges.title: Badges
badges.note: Soft background with text in the same tone, or a dot. Never a colored border.

field.title: Field
field.note: Pill on input, no border; focus with the ring.

toasts.title: Notices (toast)
toasts.note: rounded-card, no border, background and text in the type tone. Success is green.

empty.title: Empty state (AcerolaEmptyState)
empty.note: The mascot takes the round icon's place; font-black title, one sentence and one action.

screens.title: App screens
screens.lead: List, empty state, welcome and activity in the acerola-sync standard, built only with the tokens and the .ac-* classes. The mascot shows up in the empty state, the welcome and the notices.

empty.label: Empty state screen
empty.title: Nothing planned yet
empty.text: Search for a title and save it for later.

welcome.label: Welcome screen
welcome.title: Welcome
welcome.text: Your anime and manga list, synced with AniList.

error.title: Error screen
error.lead: One screen for any error: 404, 401, 403, 500, 503 and offline. On 4xx the main action goes home; on 5xx and offline it tries again. It never shows the raw error message.

landing.title: Your nerd shelf
landing.lead: Apps for people who read, watch and play: fast, good-looking and without depending on a server.

workspace.title: The workspace
workspace.reader: Comic and manga reader, desktop and Android.
workspace.sync: Anime and manga tracking with AniList sync.

connect.title: Connect
connect.text: Pair through the QR, peer to peer.

cta.title: Let's read?
cta.text: Download, pair and pick up where you left off, on your phone or your PC.

standard.title: Every project
standard.lead: Web, extension, desktop, Android or Rust: the same structure, the same git, the same hooks, the same i18n and the same design. This repository follows the standard and ships the kit to start any project.

skills.title: Three skills, one standard
skills.lead: The agent loads the right skill before touching anything, and the hooks reject whatever escapes it.

design.title: How the app looks
design.text: Tokens, typography, components, required states, accessibility, motion, copy, icon and mascot.

project.title: How the project is built
project.text: English for everything the user does not see, folder structure, layer patterns, i18n, license and new projects.

git.title: How the code moves
git.text: Commits, Git-Flow, branch guards, PRs, issues, Actions, Dependabot and releases.

english.title: What the user does not see is in English
english.lead: Folders, files, routes, variables, types, JSON and config keys, tables, columns, models, logs and code comments. Only what shows on screen is in Portuguese (through i18n); docs, skills, commits and PRs are for people and stay in Portuguese.

i18n.title: Every project has i18n
i18n.lead: Paraglide (inlang) with pt-br and en. Keys in English, nested by subject: one more level instead of _ or - to glue contexts together.

structure.title: The root belongs to the repository
structure.lead: Code lives in folders named after the commit scope. The root holds only what belongs to the whole repository.
structure.swap: They are the standard, not law: swapping one is allowed with the reason written under "Desvios do padrão" in the project's CLAUDE.md.

ui.name: Interface
ui.pattern: Dumb component (data / events / ui) and an orchestrating page

state.name: State
state.pattern: use-*.svelte.ts hook or ViewModel; no loose global state

domain.name: Domain
domain.pattern: Pure service or use case, testable without I/O

data.name: Data
data.pattern: Repository: SQL and external calls only there

platform.name: Platform
platform.pattern: Port in the domain, adapter in the infra (ports & adapters)

errors.name: Errors
errors.pattern: Typed, with a message that says what to do; never swallowed

git.title: [type](scope): Message
git.lead: Portuguese, capital first letter, no period, up to 100 characters. One scope per commit. Merges follow the format too.

branches.main: production · only the admin merges and pushes
branches.develop: integration · merges only, no direct commits
branches.feature: feature · branches off develop and goes back to it
branches.bugfix: fix · branches off develop and goes back to it
branches.release: version · goes to main and develop, tagged vX.Y.Z
branches.hotfix: urgent · branches off main, goes to main and develop

hooks.title: Lock what can be locked
hooks.lead: lefthook in git (the same for Rust, Kotlin or Node) and Claude Code hooks in the agent.
hooks.commit: guards main/develop, checks design and i18n
hooks.edit: rejects a file that escaped design or i18n

github.title: Actions and repository
github.lead: Issue and PR templates, CODEOWNERS per folder, and workflows with predictable names and triggers.

rules.files: One workflow per scope and job: <scope>-tests.yml, <scope>-release.yml, <scope>-deploy.yml
rules.triggers: Tests on push and PR to develop and main, with the scope's paths; workflow_dispatch always
rules.steps: Steps: checkout → setup with cache → install → lint → types → design → i18n → tests → build → publish
rules.secrets: Secrets in secrets, addresses in vars; optional step with if: vars.X != ""
rules.deps: Weekly Dependabot on develop, grouped, prefix [chore](deps)

license.title: MPL-2.0 on everything we own
license.lead: Code, CSS, scripts, skills, docs, icon and mascot. Third-party work keeps its original license (fonts under SIL OFL 1.1).

start.title: Five steps
start.lead: From the zip to the first commit on develop.

download.title: Download the kit
download.text: acerola-template.zip at the root of the new repository.

configure.title: Configure
configure.text: acerola.config.json: name, commit scopes, design and i18n folders.

git.title: Wire up git
git.text: node scripts/git/setup-git.mjs: Git-Flow, template and lefthook.

brand.title: Bring the brand
brand.text: theme.css + components.css, or the tokens.json theme on Android.

badRequest.title: Something in the request was off
badRequest.text: The address or the data sent came in a shape we don't understand. Check it and start over from the home page.

unauthorized.title: Sign in to continue
unauthorized.text: This page is only for signed-in accounts. Sign in and come back here.

forbidden.title: This page isn't for you
forbidden.text: Your account has no access to this. If you think it should, talk to whoever runs the app.

notFound.title: Page not found
notFound.text: The address may have changed or never existed. Go back to the start and take it from there.

timeout.title: That took too long
timeout.text: The answer didn't arrive in time. Try again in a moment.

tooMany.title: Easy, too many requests
tooMany.text: Too many requests in a short time. Wait a minute and try again.

server.title: Something broke on our side
server.text: The error was ours, not yours. Try again; if it keeps happening, come back later.

unavailable.title: Down for a moment
unavailable.text: The service is under maintenance or overloaded. Try again in a few minutes.

offline.title: You're offline
offline.text: Check your Wi-Fi or mobile data and try again.

unknown.title: Something went wrong
unknown.text: We're not sure what happened. Try again; if it keeps happening, go back to the start.
